summary: Houston County tower tied to a 1952 deer restocking release; credited to the Texas Forest Service, but a 1952 photo record places it in Davy Crockett National Forest.

events.note: Houston County deer restocking project: first load of deer released at the Shady Grove tower early in 1952, per a February 1953 newspaper item
Further shipments were planned for the winter of 1952, but trapping results were sharply curtailed; the item blames a mild winter that left deer enough natural food to skip the bait traps
1952 photo record describes the site as Shady Grove/Firetower in the Davy Crockett National Forest; creator listed as United States Forest Service

evidence.supports: Texas list credits the Houston County tower to the Texas Forest Service
tower about 10 miles southeast of Crockett, per the 1953 item
evidence.quote: Shady Grove Fire Lookout Tower about 10 miles southeast of Crockett

evidence.supports: deer project launched early in 1952; first load released at the tower
evidence.quote: The Houston County project was launched early last year when the first load of deer was released at the Shady Grove Fire Lookout Tower

evidence.supports: shipments planned for winter 1952; trapping results sharply curtailed
mild winter left natural food; deer passed up bait in the traps
evidence.quote: the deer passed up bait in the traps

evidence.supports: photo record describes the site as Shady Grove/Firetower in Davy Crockett National Forest
evidence.quote: Deer Release - Shady Grove/Firetower - Davy Crockett National Forest

evidence.supports: photo record creator is the United States Forest Service
TopoQuest places the tower in Houston County at about 31.21 N, 95.35 W

notes_for_editor: Agency conflict. The Forest Lookouts Texas list credits the Texas Forest Service. The 1952 SFASU photo record (creator United States Forest Service) places the site in Davy Crockett National Forest. Unresolved; a Davy Crockett National Forest office or Texas A&M Forest Service history record could settle it. No build date, design, height, staffing or access found. The FFLA status list shows no date that I saw. TopoQuest gives an elevation of 341 ft (not used in the story). The 1953 Grand Prairie Daily News item was read only as quoted on the Forest Lookouts page, not in the newspaper itself. No photo added: the SFASU page text read has no image URL.
